title: Partition String Into Substrings With Values at Most K
summary: Given a string s made of digits 1-9 and an integer k, find the minimum number of substrings in a partition where each digit is in exactly one substring and the value of each substring is ≤ k.
statement: Given a string s made of digits 1-9 and an integer k, find the minimum number of substrings in a partition where each digit is in exactly one substring and the value of each substring is ≤ k. Return -1 if no such partition exists. The value of a substring is its integer value, and a substring is a continuous segment of the string.
constraints: The string contains digits 1 through 9, so substrings have no leading zero.
Partition every digit into contiguous nonempty pieces whose integer values are at most k.
Return the minimum piece count, or -1 if even one digit cannot fit.
hints: Because all digits are positive, extending a piece can only increase its value.
From each position, take the longest prefix whose numeric value does not exceed k.
If the first digit already exceeds k, return -1; otherwise repeat from the first unused digit.
Any solution must cut no later than the greedy cut, so exchanging its first cut for the greedy one cannot increase the remaining piece count.
editorial: Any solution must cut no later than the greedy cut, so exchanging its first cut for the greedy one cannot increase the remaining piece count.

tests.explanation: The minimum partition 16 | 54 | 6 | 2 uses four bounded values.
Digit eight exceeds five by itself, so no valid partition exists.
